preconditions: Redis Cluster node running a stable release (8.10.3 and earlier; the fix 9a5c6e9 has not been backported)

Attacker can open a TCP connection to the cluster-bus port (base port + 10000), which is unauthenticated (the cluster bus has no auth; the unstable branch even added cluster-bus-port-protected-mode to warn of this)

evidence.vulnerable_version: Redis 8.10.3 (latest stable) and all earlier stable releases
evidence.fixed_version: unstable only (9a5c6e9, redis#16104, 2026-10-28); no stable release ships it
evidence.observed_result: The REAL redis-server is built from source at 8.10.3 (vulnerable) and 9a5c6e9 (fixed) and started in cluster mode. A crafted MEET packet (gossip count=65535, totlen=2256) sent to the cluster-bus port (port+10000) makes the vulnerable server read getPingExtLength() at hdr + 104*65535 (~6.8MB past the ~4KB receive buffer) and die with SIGSEGV (rc=-11). The fixed server logs 'Received invalid meet packet with gossip count 65535 that exceeds total packet length (2256)' and keeps serving (PONG).

real_exploit.target: Redis Cluster 8.10.3 (latest stable) — the actual redis-server binary built from source, running in cluster mode
real_exploit.backend: the real src/cluster_legacy.c::clusterProcessPacket() parser in a live redis-server process (built via make MALLOC=libc with the musl toolchain)
real_exploit.demonstrated: A single crafted cluster-bus MEET packet (16-bit gossip count set to 65535, FLAG0_EXT_DATA set) causes the vulnerable 8.10.3 redis-server to SIGSEGV (observed rc=-11, signal 11) — a remote unauthenticated crash of a Redis Cluster node. The same packet against the fixed build (9a5c6e9) is rejected with a length warning and the server survives. Differential is attributable purely to the missing 'totlen < explen' bounds check.
